# SK2009 — An enum switch omits declared members

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A switch over a non-flags enum has neither every declared value nor a catch-all arm.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

A switch that silently falls through when a new enum member is added turns a closed decision into an accidental default. Listing every value makes the compiler-visible decision explicit and makes future additions show up at the switch that needs a policy.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
return color switch { Color.Red => 1, Color.Green => 2 };
```

Write:

```csharp
return color switch { Color.Red => 1, Color.Green => 2, Color.Blue => 3 };
```

## When it does not fire

The rule excludes `[Flags]` enums, whose combinations are intentionally open, and any switch with `default`, discard, `var` or declaration catch-all handling. It also skips pattern forms other than constants and `or` combinations rather than guessing which values a relational, negated or recursive pattern covers. Enum aliases are compared by constant value, so handling one alias handles all aliases with that value. No fix is offered because the correct behavior for a missing value is a domain decision.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2009.severity`
